# Credit cards and debt

Plain-language notes on cards, balances and collectors.

## How APR works

The annual percentage rate is the yearly cost of carrying a balance. The card divides it by 365, charges that daily rate on each day's balance, and adds it to what you owe. A balance at 24% APR grows by about $20 a month for every $1,000 owed.

## The grace period

If you pay the full statement balance by the due date every month, purchases carry no interest at all. Carry any balance over and the grace period is lost until you pay in full for a cycle or two.

## Minimum payments

The minimum is mostly interest at first. Paying only the minimum on a $4,000 balance at 24% takes more than ten years and costs thousands in interest.

## Paying down several balances

The avalanche method pays the highest-APR card first and saves the most interest. The snowball method pays the smallest balance first, which gives quicker wins. Either way, pay the minimum on every card and put everything extra on one.

## Credit score basics

Payment history and the share of your limit you are using matter most. Keep utilization under 30% of the limit, pay on time, and leave old accounts open. Scores run from 300 to 850.

## Hard and soft inquiries

A hard inquiry happens when you apply for new credit and can lower a score by a few points for a few months. Checking your own score is a soft inquiry and does no harm.

## Disputing a charge

Write to the card issuer within 60 days of the statement that shows the error. The issuer must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve it within two billing cycles.

## Debt collectors

A collector must send a written notice within 5 days of first contact. You have 30 days to dispute the debt in writing, and the collector must stop until it verifies it.
